# PvP, mace and bow combat

## Faster melee pursuit and openings (1.15.7)

- **Attack rhythm.** Both melee loops struck one tick after their counter reached
  zero. A sword now hits every 13 ticks (its full 12.5-tick cooldown) instead of
  14; axes, the mace and the CPS cap likewise lose the extra tick.
- **Knockback no longer ends direct pursuit.** A hit lifts the opponent more
  than a block. That height used to count as a terrain step, handing movement to
  the navigator for 1.8 s after almost every hit. The footwork now compares the
  ground under an airborne opponent (Mineflayer does not track other entities'
  `onGround`, so a changing height marks it as airborne).
- **Sprint jumps.** On checked flat ground the bot sprint-jumps once running
  (about a quarter faster than sprinting). It jumps only if the landing stays
  short of the opponent, allowing for knockback decay, and the whole flight
  corridor is supported and hazard free. It needs sprinting, more than 6 food and
  the movement setting that allows sprint jumps (parkour, on by default).
- **Leading a runner.** Beyond reach + 1 block the bot faces a point up to half a
  second ahead along the opponent's observed velocity, if that corridor is clear.
- **Hits from below.** An opponent on a pillar or ledge within reach of the
  bot's eyes is approached on the bot's own level and hit, instead of waiting
  for a route on top. A visible opponent within reach is also aimed at and hit
  while the navigator owns movement.
- **Sprint reset.** `sprintTap` now acts on the tick after each hit. The old
  50 ms window rarely matched a tick, so later charged hits were often not
  sprint hits for the server. Pursuit also agrees with Custom PvP's sprint
  release before a falling critical instead of toggling sprint twice per tick.
- **Criticals with a shield.** Holding the bot's own shield during the weapon
  cooldown no longer cancels critical jumps; the shield is lowered on the strike
  tick. An opponent's raised shield still prevents pointless jumps.
- **Openings.** A shield blocks only after 5 ticks of use. A raise the bot saw
  begin can still be hit within `150 ms − ping`; with unknown ping or ping of
  150 ms or more this window is closed. An opponent facing more than about 100°
  away is treated like one eating or drinking (`punish`): no strafing, straight
  pressure.

`pvp-duel-benchmark.mjs` measures these changes in simulated duels. See
[the duel benchmark report](COMBAT-DUELS.md) for scenarios, results and
reproduction commands.

## Faster PvP decisions (1.15.6)

The director reuses inventory capabilities, corridor block reads, crystal damage
calculations and pearl collision bounds within each decision. Crystal plans
refresh on movement, health, block confirmations and opponent state changes.
Ready combinations resume at their action cooldown instead of waiting for the
next broad scan. Equip/aim verification always reads a fresh world state.

Measured exact pearl planning is about 2× faster, open-ground pursuit checking
2.76× faster, and continuing crystal layouts 4.28× faster. In the packet/physics
fixture, foundation → crystal → attack takes 150 ms instead of 300 ms at a
100 ms action interval. See [the benchmark report](COMBAT-PERFORMANCE.md) for
the workload, full comparison, raw summaries and reproduction commands.

## Water entry and low-ceiling sprint jumps (1.15.5)

Water entry keeps one continuous dive until physics confirms the swimming pose.
Navigation and combat jump inputs yield during entry and surface cruising, so
crouching cannot repeatedly raise the eyes and cancel the dive. Shallow water,
shore climbing, low hunger and legacy flotation retain their previous controls.

The movement setting `allowLowCeilingJumps` (enabled by default in the worker) repeats normal
sprint jumps beneath a two-block ceiling, releasing jump in the air to jump
again on landing. It works independently of parkour in mined tunnels, ordinary
navigation and either PvP engine's pursuit under leaves. It requires sprint,
food and a clear supported corridor, and yields to crouching, digging, terrain
interactions, item use, axe attacks, pearls and survival actions. Turning it off
also prevents the navigator's optional sprint hops beneath low ceilings. Saved
movement settings apply after restarting the bot. The native pathfinder option
can also be enabled or disabled with `pathfinder.setMoveOptions()`.

Physics regressions on 1.20.4 and 26.1.2 cover competing jump inputs during water
entry, enabled/disabled tunnel and canopy travel, repeated head collisions,
navigation arrival and hazards. Both PvP engines also chase from shore into
water and under leaves using the bundled worker.

## Stable melee focus and shield timing (1.15.4)

Melee aim follows the live target once per tick along the shortest yaw change,
including the -180/180 degree seam. It does not restart a smooth-look tween on
each update. The aim point remains inside the target's hitbox while jumping;
immediately before an axe strike it is checked again against actual reach and
the current view ray. The outgoing attack publishes that rotation first.

A normal critical jump keeps its checked ground corridor through the apex, so
pathfinding cannot turn the camera towards a route node halfway through the hit.
Axe cycles disable strafing, stop horizontal input for the jump and keep ownership
until landing. Auto mode retains that axe sequence. The bot holds its shield
while charging, lowers it before jumping/striking, and restores the preferred
weapon after the enemy lowers its shield. Restoring a sword waits for the real
weapon cooldown; sword and axe minimum cooldowns also correct the upstream timing
table. Without an available shield break, it holds its shield and faces a blocking
opponent without pointless critical jumps. Shield use has no delayed re-raise
callback that can survive stop, target loss or another combat mode.

`defense.test.mjs` checks default smooth aim/strafe settings with a moving target
at the yaw seam, the first charged falling axe hit, shield release at the attack,
the absence of routing at the jump apex, steady blocking and sword restoration.
These use Mineflayer physics and real versioned packet serialization on 1.20.4
and 26.1.2; they do not confirm a live server's damage or shield-disable rules.

## Continuous pursuit and committed combinations (1.15.3)

Adaptive melee sprints along checked open ground even beyond 16 blocks. When
progress stalls for 650 ms, or an obstacle blocks the corridor, navigation owns
movement and aim for at least 1.8 seconds before a clear six-block corridor can
return control to direct pursuit. Combat rotation, strafing, critical jumps and
sprint taps yield to that route. Distant entity updates use a 2–4 block margin
and at least 600 ms between replans; close escapes and large teleports update
immediately. Both attack engines retain selected enemies through the director's
allowed range, including pearl range when chase is enabled.

A crystal setup equips its next required item and starts on the selection tick.
Pending confirmations are checked each tick rather than waiting for the layout
cache. A committed base/cover sequence may finish despite a marginal score change,
with a bounded commitment; damage, health, pressure, owner and geometry checks
still apply. The configured action interval remains enforced. Confirmed crystals
finish before pearl pursuit. After a mace strike, an expired hit-confirmation
window retains the airborne controller until landing, so Auto cannot swap to an
axe or initiate another pearl in midair. Survival rescue can still take over.

With `pearlChase`, melee/auto/crystal combat also tries a safe throw at a distant
selected opponent who has never used a pearl. The threshold is
`max(8, pearlMinDistance)` and the maximum is `pearlMaxDistance`. Failed plans
continue on foot and are reconsidered at most once per 750 ms. A throw requires
a landing within 2.5 blocks of the current destination, checked again after aim.
Only one throw may be active; arrival resumes combat against the same enemy.
Explicit ranged style retains its distance unless following an enemy teleport.

## Adaptive combat director (1.15.0)

The **АГРЕССИВНЫЙ** preset enables adaptive combat, combat healing, crystal
tactics and pearl travel/escape, zero initial reaction delay, full melee skill,
fast aim and sprint resets. Inventory and the existing damage, health and travel
permission limits still apply. New settings alone do not enable crystals/pearls;
select this preset or enable those features explicitly.
Existing explicit reaction/skill settings remain editable. New configurations
default to zero reaction delay and 100% melee skill. `adaptiveCombat` can be
disabled to retain the original distance-based engine selection.

The director runs before the attack engines on every physics tick (normally
50 ms). It reads current health, damage received over the last two seconds,
distance, visibility, active enemy items, blocking, equipment and available
healing/pearls. Inventory is cached for 250 ms and invalidated by slot updates.
Decision evaluation is synchronous; it does not wait for aim, inventory swaps,
critical-hit timers or path searches. Execution still respects real weapon
cooldowns, the configured CPS, reach, visibility and the server's confirmations.

Priorities and commitments:

- At 12 HP or below, create space for healing if supplies are available. At 7 HP
  or below, survival takes priority over finishing the opponent.
- A visible, unshielded enemy reporting at most 4 effective HP within four blocks
  triggers finishing pressure when the bot has more than 5 HP. No additional
  critical jump is started for that finish; a hit still needs actual reach and aim.
- A raised shield selects the existing charged axe shield-break cycle. Enemy
  food/potion/bow use triggers pressure instead of a switch to ranged combat.
- Open, level ground uses direct forward pursuit. Close combat uses short,
  stable lateral bursts while maintaining pressure. Each diagonal corridor is
  checked for support/headroom. Walls, steps, gaps, water and unknown terrain
  remain the existing navigator's responsibility. Taking damage does not
  automatically stop forward movement or start an asynchronous critical wait.
- Auto style stays in melee up to 14 blocks, and leaves ranged mode at ten blocks.
  This margin avoids repeated swaps at one distance threshold. Mace plus wind
  charge is selected with at least 12 HP, an available launch site and a target
  within eight blocks. Airborne sequences retain ownership until completion;
  low ceilings and unavailable launches retain ordinary melee. Explicit weapon,
  ranged and crystal modes remain supported.
- Recovery chooses a checked waypoint away from the target. At six blocks of
  separation or behind cover it consumes a golden apple (including at full
  hunger) or ordinary safe food. It waits for server consumption confirmation,
  then resumes the same target without another reaction delay. Apples have a
  five-second reuse window to allow their effects to work. Ordinary hunger uses
  ordinary food. Since 1.16.0, healing and regeneration potions can take priority
  over food/apples; potion preferences are under **Выживание → Автобафы**.
  Strength, speed and fire resistance are applied when the enemy is at least
  eight blocks away, skipping existing effects. See SURVIVAL.md for confirmation,
  splash safety, cancellation and version compatibility.
- `pearlEscape` uses the existing trajectory planner to create healing distance
  when `pearlEnabled` is also enabled. Health, inventory reserve, cooldown,
  loaded terrain, safe landing and one-flight limits still apply. It does not
  require `pearlChase`. A failed pearl plan falls back to retreat on foot.
- Retreat is bounded to 2.2 seconds; a failed route returns to combat with a
  two-second retry delay. Critically low health permits a last-resort meal when
  the retreat times out. Empty supplies never start an endless retreat loop.
  Stop, target loss, death and a new command cancel queued healing and throws.

Enemy health comes only from the current version's named entity metadata,
including reported absorption. Missing values are **unknown**, not an assumed
20 HP or a guess based on hit animations. Vanilla servers or server plugins can
hide or substitute this information; the director uses distance, shields, item
use and its own health when enemy HP is unavailable. It does not treat arbitrary
scoreboard points as HP. `pvp status` includes the action and observed HP.

`combat-brain.test.mjs` covers decision priorities, unknown HP/absorption, cache
invalidation, food selection, checked footwork and a decision microbenchmark.
Combat/survival/utility tests cover retreat → confirmed meal → immediate combat,
cancellation, mode hysteresis, bounded recovery and safe escape pearls.
The microbenchmark measures only the decision layer, not pathfinding or network
latency. Live duel performance still needs verification on the intended server.

### Crystal decisions in adaptive Auto style

Carrying crystals no longer forces the bot to stay in crystal mode. It compares
feasible explosions with weapon pressure: enemy damage, self damage, known enemy
HP, recent incoming damage and the number of setup steps. It ranks an immediate
break above equal damage requiring construction, rewards a predicted lethal
blast, and prefers an immediate weapon finish over building a new base.
Nonlethal trades exceeding 65% self/enemy damage are rejected; recent burst damage
or low HP at melee distance prevents starting a foundation/cover sequence.
Lethal predictions never override minimum health, maximum self damage or owner
protection. Available lower-damage but more profitable layouts can outrank the
largest raw explosion. All geometry, prediction, armour and chain-explosion
checks remain active.

The expensive layout probe is shared by selection and execution, normally every
150 ms under pressure or 300 ms otherwise. Confirmed spawn/removal, block changes
and incoming hits invalidate it. Immediately before execution, geometry, health,
damage and profitability are checked again. The bot holds the current sequence
through bounded server confirmations and promptly breaks its confirmed crystal.
If finishing becomes unsafe/blocked it tries repositioning for up to 1.2 seconds,
then returns to weapon pressure while retaining the crystal for later safe cleanup.
An unavailable or poor setup keeps the bot attacking instead of waiting with a
crystal in its hand. Explicit **Кристаллы Края** mode remains dedicated crystal
combat and still obeys all safety limits; the profitability comparison belongs
to adaptive **Авто** mode.

### Crystal movement (1.15.2)

Layout searches use copies of the player's coordinates. They never round or
write the live physics position, so repeated planning cannot snap a walking bot
back to a block corner. Approach movement updates once per tick, and an active
turn finishes before placement takes ownership of the aim. A reachable action
holds position through its cooldown, equipment change and server confirmation.

The controller keeps a useful reposition waypoint until arrival or a bounded
three-second deadline. It only chooses positions that permit a real next action;
an unavailable layout does not trigger arbitrary sidesteps or retreats. On a
checked direct approach, less than 0.12 blocks of progress over 650 ms hands
movement to the terrain planner for at least 1.8 seconds. Reaching the desired
range releases movement before testing obstacles farther ahead.

Mineflayer Bot includes the locked published packages:

- `@nxg-org/mineflayer-custom-pvp` 1.7.16: sword tactics and bow trajectory planner.
- `mineflayer-pvp` 1.3.2: selectable basic melee combat.
- `minecrafthawkeye` 1.3.9: selectable bow trajectory planner.
- `mineflayer-armor-manager` 2.0.1: automatic armour equipment on spawn/respawn and pickup.

Documentation and implementation references:

- https://github.com/nxg-org/mineflayer-custom-pvp
- https://github.com/nxg-org/mineflayer-custom-pvp/blob/master/src/sword/API.md
- https://github.com/sefirosweb/minecraftHawkEye
- https://github.com/PrismarineJS/mineflayer-pvp/blob/master/docs/api.md
- https://github.com/PrismarineJS/MineflayerArmorManager

The attached Custom PvP source identifies itself as the scoped nxg package.
The extension installs its published build, so it does not depend on a Downloads
folder or on TypeScript compilation during installation.

## Settings

### Mace and wind charges (Java 1.21+)

Select **Ближний бой → Оружие → Булава + заряд ветра** and carry a mace and
wind charges. The mace controller works with both engine selections. It follows
the target using the normal terrain planner, finds solid ground with headroom,
jumps after braking residual horizontal momentum, then aims straight down below
its current feet and throws a charge during the initial ascent.
The shield stays in the offhand; the controller switches its main hand back to
the mace while keeping movement released until an observed upward impulse
confirms the boost. Only then does it steer toward the target, so projectile
travel and server response delay cannot make it run away from the blast point.
The server receives the current airborne position and downward look before the
charge use packet. Braking and boost confirmation each have a one-second limit;
failed launches use a one-second retry delay instead of spending more charges.

Anti-knockback preserves the server impulse for the controller's own wind jump
and Wind Burst follow-up. This is a one-use exception for an upward gust burst
near the expected launch point, with the launch's cancellation and time limit.
Melee velocity packets, unrelated explosions and unsolicited wind bursts remain
filtered. No upward velocity is invented locally.

An airborne strike requires a real descent of more than 1.5 blocks, line of sight
and eye-to-hitbox reach within the configured maximum of 3 blocks. Grounded mace
attacks use its 0.6 attack speed; wind charges respect their 500 ms cooldown.
Server damage feedback confirms a hit before continuing an observed Wind Burst
bounce. After a successful grounded landing it starts another wind jump; an
unconfirmed strike/missed launch uses a bounded recovery delay. The bot never
assumes the server accepted a strike just because an attack packet was sent.
Raised enemy shields stop the combo; Custom PvP uses a carried axe first when
shield breaking is enabled. Without charges or headroom it uses ordinary mace
attacks. Without a supported mace item it falls back to sword/axe combat.
Stop, target loss, shield defense, pearl travel and survival cancel pending actions.
Emergency MLG yields briefly to an imminent reachable smash, and can take over
when the target is out of reach, hidden or blocking.

**Защита от булавы** (`maceDefense`, on by default) extends the existing shield
controller independently of the arrow-defense switch. It predicts a descending
mace user's approach and raises the shield early, allowing for the five-tick
activation delay, while continually facing that player. It also estimates motion
from position updates when the server's velocity is stale. Grounded carriers,
trajectories passing away from the bot and attacks behind solid cover do not
trigger this defense. The same pause/resume lifecycle as arrow defense prevents
navigation and attacks from overwriting the defensive aim.

Mechanics references:

- [Mojang: Java 1.21 release notes](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-java-edition-1-21)
  (smash threshold, Wind Burst and wind-charge cooldown).
- [Minecraft Wiki: Mace](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Mace),
  [Wind Charge](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Wind_Charge),
  [Blocking](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Blocking), and
  [PvP](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial:Player_versus_Player).

### General combat settings

Open Extensions → Mineflayer Bot → PvP / Предметы. Changes apply on the next bot start.
The Novice, Normal and Expert presets change melee skill, reaction, CPS, tactics,
bow accuracy, prediction and shot interval; individual controls remain editable.

Combat is enabled by default, with manual target selection. The optional automatic
mode selects nearby visible hostile mobs, never players. Explicit commands can
target any loaded player, including an authorized owner. The bot cannot attack itself.

The melee skill slider adds skipped attack opportunities. Reaction sets the delay
before beginning an attack. CPS caps attacks, while modern Minecraft weapon
cooldowns still apply. Custom PvP supports circle/random/intelligent strafing,
jump/short-hop critical hits, sprint resets, shields, axe shield breaking and smooth
aim. Basic Mineflayer PvP uses skill, CPS, weapon, reach and shield settings; the
Custom tactics do not apply to that engine. Reach is limited to 3 blocks.
Both melee engines and crystal pursuit first search for a route without breaking
or placing terrain blocks, including one-block jumps and walking around obstacles.
Navigation digs or builds only after that search finds no route, subject to the
existing movement permissions and carried materials. A planning timeout retries
movement without treating the time limit as a reason to alter the battlefield.
Custom axe shield breaking reads active-hand metadata for the current Minecraft
version, charges the axe cooldown, jumps and strikes while falling independently
of the general critical-hit setting. Stop, target loss and bow defense cancel
the cycle. The preferred weapon is restored after the
opponent lowers its shield; an axe weapon preference stays an axe.
With only axes available, Custom PvP automatically chooses an axe even with a
sword preference and prepares a falling critical for every charged attack,
including when shield breaking and general criticals are disabled. With both
weapon types carried, selecting an axe and enabling criticals uses that same
cycle to prioritize repeated criticals. Sword combat retains its chosen critical
mode. Water/lava do not allow these criticals and use charged ordinary attacks.
ArmorManager runs even with PvP disabled. Armour swaps share the combat inventory
queue, and its offhand selection is excluded so a totem cannot replace the shield
during defense. Equipment errors are reported through the worker.
Smooth melee aiming uses a bounded turn from the current view on every tick;
bow aiming uses Custom PvP's smooth-look plugin with an easing curve without
overshoot. Both melee engines wait until the view ray reaches the enemy before
attacking. Stopping cancels pending turns.
Aim speed (`smoothAimSpeed`) is adjustable from 10% to 300% while smooth aiming
is enabled. 50% halves the turn rate and 200% doubles it. It affects both melee
and bow aiming, without changing navigation
rotation speed. The Novice/Normal/Expert presets use 50%/100%/175% respectively.
Existing settings default to 100%; changes apply on the next bot start.

Auto style approaches directly in crystal mode when placement is enabled and
crystals are carried, without first starting melee strafing or critical jumps.
On clear level ground it turns toward the enemy and walks forward, releasing
forward to stop at placement distance with a restart margin. It does not brake
backward or repeatedly strafe to center on each block. Obstacles, gaps, liquids,
unloaded terrain and elevation changes use the existing pathfinder.
When no crystals are carried it prioritizes a safe crystal break, then uses the
director's pressure/ranged decisions. With the director disabled it uses a bow
beyond melee range plus two blocks, and melee nearby.
The ranged style stays with the bow; its optional melee fallback applies when a
bow or arrows are missing. Equip a bow and normal, spectral or tipped arrows in
the inventory. Bow range is limited to 120 blocks. The offhand option is effective
only on Minecraft versions with a second hand.

Bow accuracy controls additional angular scatter; 100% removes it. This is not
a promised hit percentage. Since 1.16.2, Custom PvP with prediction enabled uses
the local `bow-aim.cjs` intercept solver. Up to 24 recent position observations
(1.2 seconds) distinguish straight running, stops, turns and repeated strafing.
Look-only packets do not refresh motion age; packet bursts are coalesced,
teleports reset the history and stale horizontal speed decays. Vertical movement
uses player gravity/drag and terrain landing checks instead of clearing Y speed.
Regular reversals can repeat within the short forecast; irregular reversals
reduce the extrapolation distance. With sparse position packets, a bounded
cycle fit requires at least two observed periods and a small residual error.
The solver favours overlapping plausible
hitboxes and uses the upper torso after recent jumps to tolerate another takeoff.
These are bounded motion heuristics, not guaranteed future player inputs.

Flight time is solved using discrete arrow gravity/drag, shooter velocity,
observation age, our measured RTT (bounded at 500 ms) and half a server tick.
Unknown ping adds no network estimate. Arbitrary server lag, another player's
ping, network jitter, potion-modified physics and future random evasions cannot
be known from these observations. The arc is checked against blocks before use.
HawkEye retains its trajectory planner; prediction off retains stationary aiming.
The controller refreshes its plan each 50 ms physics tick or fresh observation,
then recalculates immediately before release after the smooth-look call. It
rechecks target validity/range, ammo, visibility and trajectory, applies exact
local/server angles and releases within one event-loop turn. A newly blocked
shot stays drawn. The shot interval starts at the actual release time.

The controller checks visibility,
charges a bow for at least 1.2 seconds and applies the configured shot interval.
HawkEye's automatic attack/radar loops are not started: the extension owns the
bow lifecycle so engines cannot shoot concurrently or leave timers behind.
Stopping a charged bow releases it into the ground because Minecraft fires when
use is released. Target death, disappearance, distance loss and disconnect all
cancel combat. Reconnect starts a new controller; manual targets are not retained.

Run `pnpm --filter @screenlauncher/mineflayer-bot benchmark:bow` for the paired
offline comparison against the actual Custom PvP 1.7.16 planner and tracker.
The benchmark scores moving hitboxes with an independent arrow integrator;
distances, latency, cache age, failed shots and timing measurements are reported.
It does not replace a live-server accuracy test.

## Bow awareness and defense

`bowDefense` enables awareness of aiming bows/crossbows
and incoming arrows, including while following an owner. Recognition now reads
live entity updates directly, rather than waiting for the tracker cache.
`bowDefenseMode` selects early aim/draw recognition or simulated trajectories;
`bowDefenseCheckMs`, `bowDefenseRange`, `bowDefenseMargin`, `bowDefenseHoldMs`
control polling, range, expanded hit bounds and shield release delay.
`bowDefenseRequireDraw` ignores bows just held without drawing (using the
version's living entity metadata, including the offhand). Rotation/equipment/
metadata/spawn updates trigger immediate checks independent of the poll interval.
Arrow simulation includes gravity, drag, short/full bow draws and terrain.
Threats appear in the
worker status. With `shield` enabled, a shield in inventory or already in the offhand and an offhand-capable
version, the bot faces the threat and raises its shield. It releases the shield
when the threat clears. Defense interrupts offensive bow charging and crystal
actions. Releasing a bow retains protection through the predicted flight time
and packet arrival grace; `bowDefenseHoldMs` applies after that time. Incoming
arrows refresh their flight direction from movement updates, so a stale spawn
velocity cannot discard an arrow as it falls. Impact, disappearance or a passed
trajectory clears the flight hold; missing updates have a bounded timeout.
Item swaps are serialized and stale actions cannot resume over defense.
The offhand bow preference does not disable shield defense. Travel pauses and
resumes after defense. Detection does not select or attack the shooter. Stop/death/disconnect
invalidate pending equips and turns. This feature is disabled by default.

## Auto Crystal

`crystalEnabled` enables crystal tactics in auto style and the dedicated crystal
style/command. `crystalPlace` and `crystalBreak` independently allow placement
and breaking. The planner searches loaded obsidian/bedrock within
`crystalPlaceRange`, checks two blocks of air (also valid on legacy versions),
entity overlap, visible clickable faces and reach. `crystalBuildBase` allows building
an obsidian foundation from carried items. `crystalCover` allows a protective full
block between bot and explosion when it reduces predicted self damage.
It builds cover only when needed to meet the damage/health limits, rather than
adding more walls after the position is already safe.
If a raised crystal exposes the bot above a low block, cover may require a second
block supported by the first. Materials must be available; armour and cover do
not bypass the configured damage/health limits.
`crystalCoverBlock` selects obsidian, planks, cobblestone or automatic material selection.
The bot waits for server block confirmation before continuing.
Cover also applies to breaking an existing crystal. If cover would obstruct placing
the crystal, it is built after placement and before breaking; the planner checks a
visible part of the crystal above cover. New foundations prefer reachable positions
toward the target (or the bot in proximity mode) and reuse existing safe bases first.
It ranks existing positions by
`crystalPriority` (damage or proximity). It breaks confirmed server entities within
`crystalBreakRange`; it never invents entity IDs or treats a placement packet as
a confirmed spawn. Reservations bound placement retries and repeat attacks.

`crystalMinDamage` gates new placements and attacks on other crystals.
The bot remembers its confirmed placements and finishes those explosions even
when the target moves away and damage falls below that minimum. It completes
the existing crystal before constructing another layout. `crystalMaxSelfDamage`,
`crystalMinHealth` and owner protection still gate every action.
Damage uses exposure rays, difficulty, known armour/toughness, protection and resistance;
unknown equipment remains conservative. A cover block is simulated before placement;
it is not assumed to protect against later explosions in a crystal chain.
all connected loaded crystal explosions contribute to the self/owner safety
bound. `crystalProtectOwners` refuses damage to other owners (an explicitly
selected owner remains an intentional combat target). `crystalPredict` and
`crystalPredictionTicks` check both the present and predicted target position.
`crystalIntervalMs` caps construction/placement and ordinary break actions.
A confirmed crystal placed by this bot can be broken on the next tick without
waiting out that interval; repeated attacks still wait for removal confirmation.
Damage and world constraints are checked again
after equipping and aiming. The current view ray must hit the actual block face
or crystal; the placement cursor uses that same intersection. The bot stays still
while waiting for server confirmation. Unsafe/missing positions produce a rate-limited status
explaining why the bot is waiting. Default limits are preserved.
The rewrite has one managed action loop instead of independent placement,
breaking, explosion and sound-triggered loops. It uses normal Mineflayer APIs.
The selected base and cover budget persist until that cycle finishes. Cover blocks
do not become new competing foundations in the middle of the cycle.
`crystalFastAim` defaults to immediate exact rotation. With it disabled, smoothing
gets 100 ms before exact rotation; actions never await SmoothLook's sometimes
unresolved completion promise. `crystalMaxCoverBlocks` bounds cover per cycle.
`crystalSpawnTimeoutMs` and `crystalRetries` bound waiting/retries for a server
spawn. Auto style retains crystal mode while waiting, and a rejected layout gets
a temporary cooldown rather than more construction.
Foundation/cover clicks use the same confirmation deadline and retry bound.
Confirmation is checked on subsequent ticks without Mineflayer's blocking 5000 ms
block-placement wait. Rejected clicks keep combat running and select another
layout after bounded retries; blocked layouts are reconsidered after 1 second.
Confirmed crystal removal immediately frees the base for the next placement,
subject to the action interval and the same damage, health and space limits.

Approach uses forward movement with gradual turns, a stopping margin and normal
jumps over single-block steps. It does not use reverse or side inputs to brake.
Walls, liquids, unloaded ground and larger drops use the existing navigator.
If close players occupy placement space or obstruct a crystal attack, the bot
chooses a nearby standing position with usable reach, visibility and damage.
That waypoint persists while moving instead of changing direction on every tick.
Recent hits trigger faster close-range replanning. Placement and confirmation
pause movement, then a completed explosion starts the next cycle.

## Pearl travel

`pearlEnabled` is independent of the PvP master switch. `pearlFollow`, `pearlCome`
and `pearlGoto` allow throws only for their corresponding movement commands.
Follow uses the player's current position; come keeps the requested position;
auto-follow on spawn uses the same travel controller. The bot first starts its
normal route, then tries a safe throw which saves at least `pearlMinDistance`
and lands within `pearlMaxDistance` of the bot. Both shallow and lobbed arcs are
simulated tick by tick with launch velocity, inherited bot velocity, swimming
eye height, air/water drag, version-specific gravity/drag order, block and entity
collision. Throws can leave water for a dry shore. Unknown chunks, hazardous
flight paths, liquid landings,
wall impacts and landing spots without solid support or headroom are refused.

`pearlMinHealth` (minimum 6 HP), `pearlReserve` and `pearlCooldownMs` limit use.
There is at most one pearl in flight. The bot pauses navigation, equips, replans
after stopping, verifies its actual rotation/velocity again after aiming,
flushes its look packet, throws and waits for the actual position
change. It restores the held item and resumes the original goal after arrival.
If the server does not teleport it by the bounded deadline, it resumes walking
and backs off before retrying. `pearlChain` allows more throws after arrival;
otherwise each movement command can use at most one pearl. Missing pearls,
short distances or no safe route continue on foot. Stop, death, new commands
and disconnect cancel pending throws; a pearl already thrown cannot be recalled.
Projectile randomness and server plugins can change the actual landing, so
server testing is still needed for edge/platform throws.

`pearlChase` (disabled by default) enables the **ПРЕСЛЕДОВАНИЕ ЖЕМЧУГОМ**
toggle. It works with PvP enabled independently of `pearlEnabled`, which controls
ordinary travel. In addition to closing long distances, the bot recognizes the selected player's
pearl from its spawn packet and predicts its impact. Modern owner IDs are checked;
legacy ownerless packets require an unambiguous nearby thrower. Spawn velocity,
velocity updates and observed projectile movement drive the prediction.
The bot throws toward that same landing area only if a safe arc reaches within
2.5 blocks, pauses combat through its teleport and resumes against the selected
enemy. A bounded grace period preserves the target beyond ordinary combat range
and across teleport despawn/respawn. Normal cooldown, health, inventory reserve
and one-flight limits apply. Stop, target death, new targets and disconnect cancel
pending pursuit. An unreachable landing never triggers a partial travel throw.
`pearlChain` applies to movement commands; separate enemy throws can each trigger
one pursuit. The swimming/tick-order model follows the motion described by
[MinecraftMotionTools](https://github.com/OrHy3/MinecraftMotionTools) and water
drag in [projectile-trajectories](https://github.com/Bactrosaurus/projectile-trajectories).

The supplied mineflayer-ender and mineflayer-auto-crystal-rewrite sources were
used as design references for these rewritten controllers:

- https://github.com/nxg-org/mineflayer-ender
- https://github.com/nxg-org/mineflayer-auto-crystal-rewrite

No files are loaded from Downloads and no extra runtime dependency is required.

## Commands

Only launcher owners can use these commands through the configured chat/whisper
channel. Replace `!` with the configured command prefix:

- `!attack Player`: attack using the selected style.
- `!sword Player`: force melee.
- `!bow Player`: force ranged combat, with the configured fallback.
- `!crystal Player`: force crystal tactics (must be enabled in settings).
- `!attack nearest` / `!bow nearest`: select the closest loaded hostile mob.
- `!pvp auto`: enable hostile mob selection for this connection.
- `!pvp stop` or `!stop`: stop combat and suspend automatic selection.
- `!pvp status`: show the target/mode or idle status.

`come`, `follow`, `goto`, `look` and `jump` stop combat and suspend auto selection.
Run `!pvp auto` to resume it. Restarting uses the saved auto-selection setting.
Self targeting is rejected without changing the current task. Named targets must
be loaded by the server and within the configured range; a player in the tab list
alone is not enough. Combat checks line of sight through the world, without
requiring the bot to already face the target.

The classic entity-follow API used by the combat plugins is adapted to the
launcher's existing dynamic entity goals. The launcher keeps its movement
settings and supplied pathfinding rewrite; a second navigator is not loaded.

## Packaging and verification

Version 1.15.8 keeps the 1.15.7 pursuit and attack policy while reducing repeated
geometry work. A validated lead corridor is reused only when the movement check
has exactly the same start, destination, range and length. The initial six-block
check still runs in full. Ground and headroom samples reuse column results only
within one synchronous corridor check; subsequent decisions read the world again.
Pearl flight checks skip repeated samples of the same block while preserving
every sampled cell, raycast, candidate angle and entity-collision check.

The Behavior tab has an `АНТИОТБРАСЫВАНИЕ` toggle, disabled by default (also for
legacy settings). With it off, nearby players and mobs push the bot and server
hit/explosion impulses apply normally. With it on, those impulses are suppressed
while walking, jumping, falling and server position corrections remain active.
The adapter preserves native `lpVec3` speeds on newer protocols (including
1.21.11 and 26.1.2), instead of dividing those decoded speeds by 8000 again.
Save the setting and restart the bot to apply it. Server team collision rules
can still disable body pushes independently of this setting.

`pnpm test:worker` includes combat lifecycle, world visibility, melee attack and
bow tests against 1.8.8, 1.20.4 and 26.1.2 registries and a simulated world.
Knockback checks also cover 1.21.11 and verify actual player displacement after
serialized hit packets. Crystal checks simulate forward pursuit, obstacle
fallback, rejected block confirmations and consecutive placement/break cycles.
`crystal-tactics.test.mjs` covers fleeing targets, close melee pressure, occupied
placement space, entity-obstructed attacks and two stepped terraces using real
player physics and serialized placement/attack packets on 1.20.4 and 26.1.2.
`utility.test.mjs` also checks real serialized pearl throws on those versions,
safe/blocked/unknown terrain, pearl permissions/cooldown/chaining, teleport
timeout/cancellation, crystal exposure/owner safety/reservations and bow defense.
Outgoing combat packets are checked by the real Minecraft protocol serializer.
The compatibility adapter translates legacy attacks to the separate `attack`
packet on 26.1 and supplies movement flags for older plugin packet writers.
This validates API compatibility and cancellation without connecting to a user's
server. Server-specific damage, anti-cheat and real duel performance require an
in-game check on the intended server.

`pnpm package:extensions` ships the updated worker, combat configuration/code,
locked production dependencies and corresponding source in the extension ZIP.
For an existing launcher installation, install/update Mineflayer Bot through the
Extensions screen using a launcher built from this source, or use the new ZIP.

import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { readFile, readdir, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";

const require = createRequire(new URL("./pathfinding/package.json", import.meta.url));
const { build } = require("esbuild");

await build({
  absWorkingDir: fileURLToPath(new URL("../../", import.meta.url)),
  entryPoints: [fileURLToPath(new URL("./pathfinding/dist/index.js", import.meta.url))],
  outfile: fileURLToPath(new URL("./pathfinder.cjs", import.meta.url)),
  bundle: true,
  packages: "external",
  platform: "node",
  format: "cjs",
  target: "node22",
  banner: {
    js: "// Generated by pnpm build:pathfinder. GPL-3.0-only; includes MIT Rewrite code and adapted Botcraft code. See COPYING, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and pathfinder-source.json.",
  },
});

// Ship the corresponding editable source with the standalone GPL worker and
// the embedded installer. No dependency trees or build outputs go in this file.
const root = fileURLToPath(new URL("./", import.meta.url));
const files = {};
async function collect(relative) {
  for (const entry of await readdir(path.join(root, relative), { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const next = path.posix.join(relative, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) await collect(next);
    else files[next] = await readFile(path.join(root, next), "utf8");
  }
}

# Minecraft pathfinding rewrite for ScreenLauncher

This is a source copy of the supplied `minecraft-pathfinding-2026-rewrite`
(`@nxg-org/mineflayer-pathfinder` 0.0.26, GenerelSchwerz, MIT).
The supplied README is preserved as `UPSTREAM.md`; it describes the upstream
project, while this file describes the integration shipped by ScreenLauncher.

The worker uses this planner and its movement executors through the generated
`../pathfinder.cjs`. The original `mineflayer-pathfinder` package is removed from
the worker's dependencies. The downloaded source directory is left intact.

Changes from the supplied source:

- Version 1.15.5 keeps the entry dive active until swimming starts and prevents
  competing jump inputs from cancelling entry or lifting a cruising swimmer.
  The worker installs optional low-ceiling sprint jumps for navigation and direct
  pursuit, with full-footprint support/clearance checks and airborne jump release.
  The native `allowLowCeilingJumps` option can be changed with `setMoveOptions`.
  The worker enables it by default independently of parkour; disabling it
  also suppresses optional navigator head-hit jumps. Normal step, gap, climb,
  interaction and combat-action controllers retain their own jump inputs.

- Version 1.12.4 keeps the player's whole foot corridor supported through narrow
  bends. Dry diagonal moves and straight-line optimization preserve missing
  inside corners; rim handoffs retain crouch until both position and momentum
  are safe. Optional sprint hops need a supported landing and braking room
  before the next bend; airborne travel never inherits ground rim crouching.
  Open-ground sprinting retains its speed. Placement waits for real
  server confirmation instead of writing predicted blocks into Mineflayer's
  live world. Background placements retain their completion/error tracking.
  Rejected or inaccessible placement cells are excluded for the current goto,
  so recovery plans toward the original destination from real terrain rather
  than repeating a failed stair. Physics regressions on 1.20.4 and 26.1.2 cover
  G-shaped one-block walkways in both directions, crouched outside rims and a
  canopy-covered forest with a rejected placement and delayed confirmations.

- Version 1.12.3 gives ready traversal routes priority over construction with
  digging/building enabled. The read-only probe includes every enabled parkour,
  Neo, momentum and ladder provider, and runs before overhead construction even
  when digging is disabled. Construction can reuse Neo and ladder movements too.
  After repairing an initial gap, a read-only continuation avoids building around
  the rest of an already usable course. Ordinary jumps retain control until real
  supported landing before handing off to the next move. Physics regressions
  cover ready mixed courses on 1.20.4 and 26.1.2, necessary first-gap repair and
  ladder-assisted climbing with a full scaffold inventory.

- Version 1.12.2 extends construction planning across the full approach, tower,
  bridge and platform landing, including level and lower offset platforms.
  Its bounded search prices missing bridge floors and uses ordinary gap jumps
  when enabled, without running expensive ice/Neo simulations for every scaffold
  branch. Existing routes and ice approaches retain priority. Bridge placement
  approaches an exposed support face while crouching and confirms the real block
  before using it as a floor or another placement anchor. Unfinished interactions
  cannot complete a walking move; diagonal bridging respects the remaining stock.
  Physics tests cover long straight and diagonal bridges, tower-to-bridge travel,
  a lower platform, limited-block jump exits and delayed placement confirmations.

- Version 1.12.1 tries existing open mine passages before planning a new exit.
  Nearby overhead goals use a bounded construction search that validates the
  whole tower and its platform exit together, respecting inventory, headroom,
  protected floors and exclusions. Incomplete climbs retain efficient multi-step
  ascents instead of stopping at the first rise. Ordinary walking releases stale
  crouch input after corner or placement alignment. Physics regressions cover a
  mine entrance facing away from the owner, a twenty-block tower and continuous
  sprint through merged and short waypoints.

- Version 1.8.12 applies the supplied Baritone 26.1 ascent, descent and partial
  search approach to Mineflayer. One-block jumps align laterally and respond to
  actual ground contact, with another attempt after a failed takeoff. Ascents
  and descents retain control until supported arrival. Jump optimization keeps
  turns and checks the body's clearance on straight continuations. Corner
  correction reaches the route's entry waypoint; forward alignment releases
  opposing controls. Horizontal alignment is normalized after removing height.
  Verified dry routes found during shore selection are retained and executed
  after landing, provided their endpoint still satisfies the current goal.
  Retries increase the search budget for come/goto too. Partial search prefers
  affordable progress from the start, and repeated prefixes cannot cycle
  indefinitely. A timed-out mountain search can execute a short supported dry
  ascent, including allowed scaffolding or digging, then continue toward the
  original player from the new height. A bounded uphill detour can move sideways
  beneath an overhead target without discarding the elevation already gained.
  Planned terrain edits stay on their own search branch and survive excursions
  outside the local cache, preventing phantom openings and removed landings.
  Repeated motion without waypoint progress
  triggers replanning.
  Ready momentum flights install their controls immediately after optimization, so
  catch-up physics ticks cannot consume an incoming ice takeoff while idle.
  Physics regressions cover grassy steps, flowers, trenches, wall turns, and
  water-to-mountain routes on 1.20.4 and 26.1.2.
  Failed placements/mining propagate to movement recovery and cannot mark an
  absent block as a finished interaction. Background interactions deliver their
  errors through the movement runner. A swimmer retreats out of a future shore
  step before placing it, then awaits the server-confirmed block before climbing.

- Version 1.8.11 checks the onward route when selecting a water exit, so a
  nearby isolated ledge does not win over a usable mountain approach. Probes
  share the real movement rules, inventory and planned shore placement, with
  small cancellable search budgets. Swimming strokes keep forward propulsion
  rather than applying land braking toward a waypoint below breathing height.
  Dynamic following survives search timeouts and blocked movement, increases
  its search budget on retries and wakes on target or terrain changes. Idle
  following also checks displacement and replaced entity position vectors.
  Come/goto retry transient route failures twice and still report permanent
  failures. Arrival is checked against the actual position after execution or
  recovery. Mining/API failures keep their existing error behavior.
  Walking shortcuts sweep the full player body through collision shapes;
  off-centre turns first reach their supported approach waypoint. A blocked walking
  or swimming step triggers replanning, and water bobbing is not progress.
  Pearl pursuit evaluates rotations rounded by Mineflayer before comparing
  safe landing arcs, including a retry after drifting during water aiming.

- Version 1.8.4 retains swimming momentum across partial route searches in open,
  loaded water. Prefix completion uses the reached water column at the actual
  swimming height. Reached waypoints and late camera callbacks cannot reverse
  the next stroke. Arrival, cancellation and interactions still release travel
  controls. Physics predictions copy server attributes, preserve speed modifiers
  and use the live grounded state for takeoff acceleration. Ordinary parkour
  controls commit takeoff on every physics tick, including catch-up ticks, and
  brake on landing. Short run-ups retreat along the flight line and finish
  settling before accelerating; aiming preserves the nearest landing axis.
  Regression routes cover four empty blocks, four-by-four diagonal jumps,
  lag catch-up, sustained ocean speed and parkour after leaving water.

- Water travel uses sprint swimming on modern versions: a brief dive starts the
  swim pose, then the bot swims at the surface and releases jump while breathing.
  The live water simulation uses Botcraft physics with fluid-free pose clearance
  and retains swim sprint while the eyes are above water. Idle, shallow water,
  shore collisions and low hunger use standing flotation. The overlay restores
  controls and physics on disposal; legacy versions keep water-jump movement.
  Consecutive water moves retain forward/sprint and a level viewing pitch, so
  route transitions do not interrupt swimming or push the bot toward the sky.
  Horizontal strokes complete at the current swimming height within the same
  water column, instead of braking until the bot sinks to the planned depth.
  When an existing shore landing is beside a proposed step at the same height,
  the bot uses the landing directly; taller walls still allow a built exit.
  Reused partial routes recognize a step already confirmed by the server rather
  than waiting indefinitely for a fresh placement handler to finish.

- Version 1.5.1 keeps the Neo camera facing its landing floor while turning
  around the wall. Back and strafe inputs preserve flight acceleration without
  backward camera turns; the planner bounds rotation between airborne ticks.
  Water exits can build a supported step against a shore or bridge pillar,
  then use ordinary dry towers to reach a higher player. Building respects
  inventory, placement settings and exclusions, without requiring digging.

- Version 1.5.0 adds STAY ON WATER in BEHAVIOR (enabled for new and legacy
  settings). A disposable input overlay holds normal Mineflayer water-jump
  controls while swimming, including when navigation ends or clears controls.
  It releases its override on land, death and disconnect. High falls into open
  water are allowed independently of MAX GROUND DROP, with water depth and
  headroom checks. Water landings cannot be merged with later swimming moves;
  the bot brakes over its landing column, resurfaces and can swim onto an island.

- Version 1.4.0 adds a TypeScript adaptation of Botcraft's vertical movement
  and velocity correction. Ordinary ladders, wall vines, twisting and weeping
  vines have explicit entry, ascent, descent and ledge-exit moves. Thin ladder
  shapes are not treated as solid landing floors. Straight-line optimization
  cannot replace a climbing phase. Climbing also works with parkour disabled.
- Native Mineflayer physics and predictive Botcraft physics recognize twisting
  and weeping vine segments and tips. Climbing goals hold their height rather
  than waiting three seconds for a nonexistent ground contact.
- Concurrent chunk/goal reset requests are coalesced and settled before a new
  route starts. Superseded optimizer listeners retire before their watchdog runs.
- Supported goal completion and velocity braking avoid premature flight
  completion and running off the far edge of a narrow landing. Descending
  parkour tests a feasible walk-off before simulating extra jumping approaches.
  Drops measure the actual fall to the landing surface, honor the configured
  maximum inclusively, and check the destination headroom at its correct column.
- Follow movement faces the route waypoint, uses the player's height for pitch
  on land, and retains yaw at a reached waypoint.
  Jump aiming stays horizontal and specialized Neo flight controls keep their yaw.

- Stable Mineflayer 4.37.1 `physicsTick` execution, with one asynchronous step
  in flight at a time; no custom Mineflayer fork, Atomics busy waiting or private
  Node microtask draining is required.
- Worker search budgets: 5 ms per slice, 2.5 seconds per search and 20,000 retained
  nodes. Search yields to the event loop without waiting 50 ms for a physics tick.
  After 30 ms, a route that makes progress can start with up to 16 verified moves,
  then replan from the actual position. Exhausted budgets produce errors.
- Neo movement is integrated from Rewrite's standalone example geometry. Its
  executor searches a bounded flight with Mineflayer's own prismarine-physics,
  including a short run-up, escape-side selection, turning and landing. Flight
  controls advance synchronously for every physics tick, including catch-up ticks.
- Forward, diagonal and asymmetric gap jumps, raised and lowered landings, and
  the ladder/ladder-landing/around-corner example modules are registered by default.
  Ladder-only providers skip ordinary gap jumps and apply exclusion-zone costs;
  ladder prediction uses the real Mineflayer physics. Around-corner moves retain
  physics feasibility checks instead of executing an unverified fallback.
- Follow retargeting finishes an airborne jump before changing its destination.
  Jump input stays held until takeoff is observed. Executor state resets between
  moves, and recovery attempts and landing waits have finite bounds.
- Block-event subscriptions share one emitter listener. Chunk-sized update bursts
  debounce per position without creating temporary subscriptions. Disposing a
  callback is idempotent, and one-shot callbacks can be removed by their original
  function. The emitter's listener limit is unchanged.
- Empty paths, waiting follow goals, cancellation, rapid goal replacement,
  execution errors and disconnects release task state, controls and listeners.
- Final moves wait until the bot actually reaches the goal. Stalled movement
  reports an error after three seconds without progress in the worker.
- Euclidean `GoalNear` radius, a radius-aware heuristic and correctly floored
  `GoalBlock` coordinates. Follow validity and composite validity use `isValid`.
- Incremental LRU block updates and evictions preserve unrelated entries;
  unloaded block state queries return `undefined`; world listeners can be disposed.
- Worker settings control sprinting, parkour, digging and maximum drops.
  Placement and towers retain the previous worker's defaults and require
  inventory blocks. Unlimited liquid drops are disabled to honor the drop limit.

The 1.4.1 worker also handles jumping into head-height ladders, diagonal entries
and standing on a final ladder rung before jumping onto a higher wall. Ordinary
ladder entries and exits use the climbing controller even with parkour enabled.
One-block ground jumps include both ascent and landing in their cost, so an
adjacent bush does not get an artificial advantage over the ladder. Digging
preserves climbable blocks and the walls their ladders are attached to; other
obstacles remain diggable when the movement setting allows it.

Worker 1.6.0 stages high follow goals through a loaded, reachable shoreline when
starting in open water. After reaching dry ground it resumes the original goal,
using supported stairs, towers and bridges when inventory blocks permit it.
Adjacent ground stairs are placed from a crouched rim, then from outside the
new block before jumping. Mining costs include the selected tool, helmet
enchantments, water and unsupported footing, so a short build can beat a slow
survival tunnel. Unreachable placement faces and cancellation have bounded waits.

MomentumJump predicts both the runway and flight with Mineflayer's native
physics, including surface friction, current velocity and potion effects. It
preserves incoming speed and searches the timing of preparatory sprint-jumps,
including hops from a stone runway onto a short ice rim. A longer runway can
use several hops before the ice. The solver prioritizes landing at the ice edge
and rebounding on the immediately following tick. The
run-up and final flight are one movement, including four-air-block gaps that
would otherwise use standing parkour alignment. A bot stopped at the ice rim
can back up along the available runway before starting the same sequence.
If a rim rebound is impossible, a verified running takeoff remains available.
Controls advance
on every physics tick; jump is released during flight to reset its cooldown.
Live prediction retains the actual ground state, velocity and jump cooldown,
and rechecks exclusion zones when choosing a flight. Ice does not guarantee
five air blocks from rest: an isolated two-block ice platform is still rejected
without enough incoming speed or a usable runway. Parkour/sprint settings apply.
Long rising jumps that the standing executor cannot reliably perform are
replaced by further supported construction.

### Ice momentum calculation

The native engine is `prismarine-physics` 1.11.1; see its
[movement and jump implementation](https://github.com/PrismarineJS/prismarine-physics/blob/master/index.js).
At 20 physics ticks/second, one tick is 50 ms. For a straight sprint without
effects, a grounded tick uses `f = 0.91 * slipperiness`,
`a = 0.98 * 0.13 * 0.1627714 / f^3`, then `dx = vx + a + J` and
`vx_next = f * dx`. `J = 0.2` only on a successful sprint-jump, otherwise zero.
In the air, `f = 0.91`, `a = 0.98 * 0.026`, and there is no new jump impulse.
The engine also integrates vertical motion and the player's collision box;
horizontal distance alone is insufficient to prove a landing.

Minecraft 26.1 uses the supporting collision block under the player's feet,
not necessarily the block below their center. Verified against the official
26.1.2 client (`Entity.checkSupportingBlock`, `Entity.getOnPos`,
`LivingEntity.travelInAir`), the last grounded edge tick can still use ice
friction after the center passes the ice face. Prismarine-physics samples only
the center, which incorrectly discarded that momentum and overestimated the
needed runway. `supportingBlockPhysics.ts` supplies the supporting full block's
friction to both predictions and live physics on 26.x. It retains the real
collision shapes, never adds a floor, and leaves older protocol behavior alone.
The support is carried between ticks and invalidated when position changes.

| Surface | Slipperiness | Ground velocity multiplier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stone | 0.6 | 0.546 |
| Ice, packed ice, frosted ice | 0.98 | 0.8918 |
| Blue ice | 0.989 | 0.89999 |

Legacy reproducible example from rest, tested with the native Mineflayer physics
plugin on 1.19.4: stone at x=0..12, blue ice at x=13..14, **five empty columns** at
x=15..19, landing at x=20..23; every floor has y=63 and z=0. Start at
(0.5,64,0.5). The solver sprints for ten ticks, then chains three preparatory
hops. It touches blue ice at x=14.999206 with vx=0.283828 blocks/tick and jumps
again on the immediately following tick (50 ms after contact). The final
12-tick flight lands at x=20.084907: **5.085701 blocks of center displacement**.
These coordinates and velocities are simulation results, not injected speed.
Other tested fixtures cover ordinary, packed and frosted ice with a five-block
ice rim, taking off within two ticks of landing. Timing is recomputed for the
actual position and velocity; these example numbers are not movement constants.

The single-ice fixture matching the rim setup uses stone at x=0..5, ice at x=6,
four empty columns x=7..10, and a two-block landing x=11..12. From x=0.5, the
simulated approach lands at x=6.877939 with vx=0.259289, then jumps on the next
tick without braking. Executed tests cover all four ice types and directions,
and starting from rest on the ice itself. The latter must first back up; its
run-up is selected and rechecked against the actual position and velocity.

The ice contact is an intermediate landing: proximity completion and dynamic
follow updates cannot interrupt the active approach/rebound sequence. They can
resume after reaching the opposite platform. A partial walking route ending on
an exposed ice rim is also held until the search verifies its continuation;
otherwise it would run to the ice, consume momentum, crouch, and stop there.

The user's saved platform has stone x=0..6, ice x=7, five empty columns x=8..12,
and a landing starting at x=13. With 26.1 supporting-block friction this setup
has a verified straight approach. A shorter setup also works from centered
rest: stone x=0..2, blue ice x=3, five empty columns x=4..8, landing at x=9.
The search starts its first preparatory hop at tick 2, lands at the ice edge,
then rebounds on the next tick. Tests execute three such short runways in
sequence, in all four directions, with forward view and no intermediate stop.

The executor checks the live position, velocity and jump cooldown before
installing controls synchronously at the physics boundary. When retreating
along the runway it faces the safe route before moving, including when the
player's center has slid past the ice face. Blocked takeoffs wait for a verified
route instead of consuming a runway prefix.

Preparation now predicts a short held movement followed by coasting and joins
that sequence directly to the verified flight. It checks the launch position
and live speed together, instead of alternating opposite keys to stop within
two millimetres of one coordinate. Longer retreats use walking speed; crouching
is reserved for the final approach. Small lateral offsets are accepted when the
whole trajectory still lands safely. Unchanged controls are held across ticks.
If coasting alone cannot hit a viable tick phase, preparation can include one
planned braking reversal. The live ice contact also retains at least 98% of
the planned contact speed, so early alignment cannot replace a strong rebound
with a marginal slower jump.

View changes also update Mineflayer's transmitted look immediately, and the
landing restores the forward view. The search refines straight approaches before
trying optional 45-degree air inputs. These use forward+right with a rotated
view so acceleration still follows the runway, while sprint-jump impulses stay
straight. Where those inputs are necessary, it returns the
view forward as early as native collisions allow, retaining at least 0.005 blocks
of pre-landing overlap or the original candidate's overlap if smaller. It never
decouples the simulated direction from the view sent to the server.

`allowAirStrafe` defaults to `false` in the worker, launcher settings and movement
options. The launcher exposes it as **TURN HEAD DURING JUMPS**. With it disabled,
both planning and live execution use straight input and view; a jump requiring
45-degree air inputs is rejected rather than turning anyway. Enabling it opts
into the additional native input candidates described above.

Consecutive collinear ice jumps are verified as one movement, using each native
landing's position and velocity to calculate the next approach (up to eight
gaps per candidate). Their controls share one synchronous tick queue, so an
intermediate landing does not clear sprint, crouch or stop at a block center.
The executor settles after the last jump, then normal routing continues to the
followed player, including updates received during the chain. Partial routes
ending near an unverified ice gap wait even when their prefix already includes
a momentum jump. Tests cover three consecutive jumps in all four directions
with straight view, a moving owner, opt-in five-air-column chains and a blocked
second takeoff. A saved eight-block first runway, six-block middle runway and
two five-air-column gaps also pass with straight view. If a landing at a block
center prevents the next short-runway takeoff, the planner tries four bounded
landing offsets within that block and verifies the resulting native velocity
against the following jump before selecting one.

The [parkour wiki's jumping analysis](https://www.mcpk.wiki/wiki/Jumping)
describes a 12-tick level jump, a 0.2 sprint-jump impulse, and resetting the jump
cooldown by releasing jump. Its [slipperiness analysis](https://www.mcpk.wiki/wiki/Slipperiness)
gives ground speed retention as `0.91 * slipperiness`: 0.8918 on ordinary ice
and 0.89999 on blue ice. [45-degree inputs](https://www.mcpk.wiki/wiki/45_Strafe)
normalize acceleration to 1.0 rather than 0.98. These explain why a single ice
block preserves incoming hop momentum but does not create an arbitrary boost.

Run-up limits are geometry and speed dependent. In the tested 26.1.2 level,
one-block-wide blue-ice fixture, starting centered at rest without effects or
a ceiling, two ordinary blocks plus ice already produce a verified straight
five-empty-column crossing; one ordinary block plus ice does not. Three ordinary
blocks plus ice also pass, including consecutive jumps. These are bounded solver
results for those starting conditions, not a universal minimum or maximum.
Already arriving with speed, other surfaces, headhitters and effects change the
range. Legacy 1.19.4 tests retain the older eight-block, opt-in 45-degree setup.
The planner tests each available runway and input timing through collisions.

Dry traversal remembers up to 4096 grounded/climbable cells for the current
connection and dimension. When an ordinary search exhausts its budget in a broad
cave, a bounded retry narrows exploration to corridors near those visited cells.
All movements are regenerated with the current terrain, enabled providers and
exclusions; memory never implies a reversible drop or a crossing through a
blocked/unloaded cell. A same-level exit can reconnect to a fresh dry route when
the owner has moved beyond the remembered area. Complete ordinary routes take
priority, so new cave shortcuts can replace older detours. Respawn and dimension
changes clear the hints. Mining also probes ready passages for horizontal and
upward approaches before excavating.
Descent smoothing merges only collinear horizontal steps, preserving the turn
where a staircase meets a cave instead of steering diagonally across its rim.

Component-based item enchantments are exposed to Mineflayer/dependency plugins
as named `{ name, lvl }` arrays. The adapter resolves component registry IDs,
keeps command-provided levels and supports stored enchantments in books, while
preserving original wire components and legacy NBT. Inventory updates install
the getter for items received after an empty login; the update listener is
removed on disconnect.

Commands from the repository root:

```powershell
pnpm build:pathfinder
pnpm test:pathfinder
pnpm test:worker
pnpm package:extensions
```

Commit the rebuilt `pathfinder.cjs` with source changes. Tauri embeds it together
with `worker.cjs`, the manifest and the npm lockfile; production installs use
`npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts` and do not compile TypeScript. The standalone
extension archive uses the same files and dependency lockfile.

The upstream package declares MIT; its supplied directory had no license file,
so the standard MIT text and named author are included in LICENSE. The combined
worker/pathfinder now uses GPL-3.0-only because of the Botcraft adaptation.
COPYING, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and the corresponding editable source bundle are
included in both the archive and embedded extension installer.
Its external physics and utility packages
(`@nxg-org/mineflayer-physics-util`, `@nxg-org/mineflayer-util-plugin`) declare
GPL-3.0 in their distributed manifests and retain their own license files.

Validation includes planning, block changes, exclusion zones, simulated movement
through Mineflayer's real physics plugin, dynamic follow cancellation and bundled
worker execution on Minecraft 1.20.4 and 26.1.2. Parkour fixtures include a 10-by-1
strip with a two-high wall in four orientations, a blocked escape side, a two-block
long wall, a moving player during the flight, ordinary up/down/diagonal gaps and
a ladder-assisted landing two blocks higher. No live server was used; latency,
server corrections and anticheat can affect a physically possible jump.

minecraft-pathfinding :tm:

A pathfinder to get a Minecraft bot from point A to point B with unnecessarily stylish movement

> [!WARNING] > This pathfinder is still in **HEAVY** development. It is not meant to be used in production. However, you can use the code in `examples` to understand how the pathfinder works.

Why use this pathfinder?

----- Presently, its execution is better than both Baritone's and mineflayer-pathfinder's. It also follows an entirely different paradigm - each move's execution is split into individual parts, which combined with a modular movement provider/executor/optimizer system, it makes this pathfinder ***extremely*** customizable. So as long as a single movement's execution handles all entry cases (which is possible), it can be immediately integrated into this bot. Examples will be added as the project undergoes more development.

What is left to be done?

----- **Many** things. - [X] Proper breaking of blocks (Cost + Execution) - [X] Water movement - [X] Parkour - [X] Proper jump sprinting - [ ] Offloading the world thread
